raw_response:
I am 66 this year, and I have been working this land since I was 16. I finished middle school, which around here means I can read a pesticide label and do my own sums, but most of what I know I learned from my father and from watching which neighbor's field looks greenest. My whole farm is 5 mu, just me and my wife now. The children are in Shijiazhuang working factory jobs, so I cannot afford a bad year — there is no one else to send money home if I lose the crop.

Last year I planted 4 mu of cotton and 1 mu of mungbean on the east corner. The cotton gave me about 500 jin per mu, and I sold it for a bit over 3 yuan per jin. This year I will keep the same layout because changing anything on a 5-mu farm is gambling, and I do not gamble with my living.

For the **cotton on 4 mu**: I will sow the improved variety that Old Wang across the ditch used last year — his bolls were fat and he got 550 jin per mu. I need 3 jin of seed per mu, so 12 jin total, which cost me 180 yuan from the dealer. For the bottom fertilizer, I will spread one 50 kg bag of 15-15-15 compound fertilizer per mu before rotary tillage — that is 4 bags, 520 yuan. At flowering time I will topdress with urea, 20 kg per mu, so 80 kg total. That is another 160 yuan. I know some people say I should put more potash, but I have been doing it this way for ten years and it works. I would rather spend a little too much on fertilizer than see my leaves turn yellow like Liu's did last year when he tried to save 50 yuan — he lost 100 jin per mu. I will irrigate three times: once before sowing in late April, once at flowering in early July, and once when the bolls are filling in August. Each time the electric pump costs about 50 yuan. For spray, cotton is hungry for medicine. I will spray 12 times from June to September — bollworm, aphids, red spider mite. Each spray is 15 yuan for the chemical, so 180 yuan total. I do rotary tillage every spring, 50 yuan per mu. If the weather is normal, I expect 550 jin per mu, which is 275 kg.

For the **mungbean on 1 mu**: I plant it on the lighter soil by the east path. Mungbean makes its own nitrogen, so I do not give it much. I put down 5 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as a base, just to get it started — that is one small handful per hole, about 5 kg total, 13 yuan. Seed is 2 jin per mu, cheap stuff, 14 yuan. I irrigate twice: once after sowing, once when the pods are plumping. I spray three times for pod borer. I expect about 200 jin per mu, which is 100 kg. The mungbean is for home eating and a little cash; I do not count on it for big money.

I keep a close eye on costs. The cotton alone will cost me almost 1,100 yuan in fertilizer, water, and spray. If I get 550 jin per mu and the price holds at 3.5 yuan per jin, the 4 mu will bring in about 7,700 yuan. After costs, that is my living and my wife's medicine. The mungbean is a buffer — I can eat it if the cotton price drops. I am not changing anything this year. What worked before will work again.
